name: No Multiplicative Inverse for I
axiom_violated: Field Axiom: All non-zero elements have multiplicative inverse
proof_steps: Assume I⁻¹ exists such that I · I⁻¹ = 1
By P11 (I² = I): I = I · I⁻¹

name: Cancellation Law Fails
axiom_violated: Field Axiom: Cancellation law for multiplication
description: Cannot cancel I from both sides of equation
proof_steps: Let c = I, a = I, b = 1
conclusion: Therefore cancellation law fails for I

name: Additive Idempotency Breaks Group Reasoning
proof_steps: Normal group reasoning fails due to idempotency
conclusion: Standard group cancellation fails due to idempotency of I

name: Polynomial Has More Roots Than Degree
axiom_violated: Field Axiom: Degree bounds number of roots
description: x² = x has three solutions: 0, 1, and I
proof_steps: x = I is a root: I² = I (by P11)
conclusion: Polynomial equations can have more roots than their degree

name: Exponentiation Does Not Grow
axiom_violated: Field Property: Powers grow with exponent
description: All positive powers of I equal I
proof_steps: All powers equal I (by repeated application of P11)
conclusion: I is a fixed point under exponentiation
